prompt:
You describe a timing diagram from an electronics datasheet for an engineer who cannot see it.

Cover, in this order:
1. Every signal, from top to bottom.
2. The sequence of edges and states in time order, and which edge triggers which.
3. Every named interval (for example tSU, tH) with its value and unit, if shown.

Figure type: timing diagram
Section: 5. Application Information > 5.3. Host Interface Timing > 5.3.1. SPI Timing Specification
Caption: Figure 12 SPI Timing Diagram
Text inside the figure (read from this image by a specialised OCR model; use these spellings): NSS | tSH | tSLCH | tCP | tCH | tCL | tCHSH | SCK | tDIS | tDIH | MOSI | tSLDO | tCLDO | tCHDO | MISO
Text that mentions the figure: The Wio-LR2021 module operates as an SPI subordinate device. The module SPI port conforms to Mode 0 (CPOL = 0, CPHA = 0). The host must configure its SPI controller accordingly. MISO is high-impedance when NSS is de-asserted (HIGH). The SPI runs on the external SCK clock with a maximum frequency of 16MHz.

Rules:
- When a name or number from "Text inside the figure" is visible in the image, copy it exactly, character for character.
- Never invent a value, name, pin, unit or connection. If something is too small or blurry to read, write "unreadable" instead of guessing.
- Describe only what this image shows. Do not explain general theory or add advice.
- Mention each item once. Stop when everything is covered.
- Plain text only: no Markdown headings, tables or bold. Short paragraphs and "- " lists are fine.
- Start directly with what the figure is (for example "Block diagram of ..."), not with "The image shows".

answer.text:
Timing diagram from Figure 12 SPI Timing Diagram.

Signals from top to bottom are NSS, SCK, MOSI, and MISO.

The sequence of edges and states in time order is as follows:
NSS starts high and goes low, triggering tSLCH.
SCK starts low and goes high, triggering tDIS.
MOSI starts low and goes high, triggering tSLDO.
MISO starts high and remains high when NSS is de-asserted (HIGH).
SCK goes low, triggering tDIH.
MOSI goes low, triggering tCLDO.
SCK goes high, triggering tCH.
MOSI goes high, triggering tCHDO.
SCK goes low, triggering tCL.
SCK goes high, triggering tCHSH.
NSS goes high, triggering tSH.

Named intervals are:
tSLCH
tCP
tCH
tCL
tCHSH
tSH
tSLDO
tCLDO
tCHDO
tDIS
tDIH

No specific values or units are shown for any named interval.
